audience.programmeDescription: Linguistics at the University of Amsterdam studies how languages are structured, acquired, processed and used. Students learn a modern language, analyse speech and meaning, and complete an independent research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two related options. One studies language and cognition with experimental and computational methods. The other studies discourse, literature and media. UvA provides a deeper sequence in linguistic structure, analysis of speech and language research.

mapping.notes and rows: Reviewed all 25 external components, 37 UCR titles, both schedules, the alignment blocks and rows, and ten course and audience notes. Czech is an illustration of the required language choice. Free electives and thesis entry remain distinct. The optional UCR project sits outside both schedules and the required UvA thesis.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

MCCCOMM112.name: Dutch
MCCCOMM112.text: This course aims to develop basic skills and strategies necessary to successfully handle uncomplicated oral and written communication in Dutch in a variety of social situations that you may encounter in daily life in the Netherlands. The emphasis in the course will be on speaking in Dutch in day-to-day situations on the one hand and understanding Dutch culture on the other hand. At the end of the course students can orally express and write about themselves in Dutch, who they are, describe their family background, and interact with others in a simple way.
